lines.text: Vera, I'm “bank”. Am I money, or a riverside?
lines.say: Vera, I'm the word bank. Am I money, or a riverside?

lines.text: Depends on the words before you: a river, or a loan.
So I ask around?
Yes. That asking around is attention.
Every token makes a query: what am I looking for? A key: what do I offer? A value: what I hand over.
Each key is matched with the query for a score. Softmax turns scores into weights that sum to one.
So I take a mix of their values, mostly from the best matches?
Yes: a weighted mix, added onto your own vector.
Try this one: “The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired.”
lines.say: Try this one: The animal didn't cross the street, because it was too tired.

lines.text: “It” looks at “animal”.
Now swap in “wide”.
Now it's the street!
Hand-set patterns, mirroring ones found in real models.
lines.say: Hand set patterns, mirroring ones found in real models.

lines.text: Wait. “Tired” comes after “it”!
Right, it can't. Tokens only look back; later words settle it.
No peeking ahead means one pass can train every position at once.
One pattern per layer?
Many, side by side: heads. GPT-2 small has 12 per layer.

lines.text: One watches the previous word, one links verbs to their doers, one tracks pronouns.
A team of highlighters!
What's the catch?
Each token checks every one before it. Double the text, about four times the work.
That square makes long contexts hard, and so much engineering fights it.
Can I try it myself?
Open the Attention chapter, click the tokens, flip tired to wide.
Tokens talking to tokens. My kind of party.
